title: ServiceNow for Financial Services: SOX, PCI-DSS, and Basel III Implementation Guide
excerpt: Implement ServiceNow in regulated financial environments with proven patterns for SOX compliance, PCI-DSS controls, and Basel III operational risk management.
content:
Financial Services Operations (FSO) Overview

ServiceNow Financial Services Operations (FSO) provides a unified platform for banking, insurance, and investment operations, enabling seamless customer experiences through advanced case management, workflows, and data models.

  • Banking: Loan origination, dispute resolution (Visa integration), payment operations
  • Insurance: Claims processing, ACORD-compliant data model
  • Investment: Trade operations workflows

FSO leverages core tables like sn_bom for financial products, customers, and transactions, supporting compliance-heavy environments in financial services.

SOX Compliance Implementation

ServiceNow's GRC module delivers proven SOX results by automating control testing, evidence collection, and continuous monitoring:

  • 66% reduction in quarterly control certification time
  • 90% reduction in external auditor coordination
  • $500,000 annual savings (ServiceNow internal data)

To implement SOX controls, administrators often query GRC-related tables for risk assessments and certifications. For example, use a GlideRecord script to retrieve active SOX controls from the sn_grc_control table, ensuring only certified records are pulled for reporting.

var gr = new GlideRecord('sn_grc_control');
gr.addQuery('state', 'IN', '1,2'); // Active controls
gr.addQuery('control_family', 'SOX');
gr.query();
while (gr.next()) {
    gs.info('Control: ' + gr.getValue('short_name') + ' - Owner: ' + gr.getDisplayValue('owned_by'));
}

This script helps SOX teams audit controls programmatically, integrating with scheduled jobs for automated quarterly reviews. Additionally, for SOX evidence collection, a business rule on the control test table can automatically attach audit logs when tests complete.

PCI-DSS Controls

ServiceNow enforces PCI-DSS requirements through native security features, GRC policy management, and FSO extensions for financial data handling.

  • Requirement 7: Restrict access using ACLs and roles
  • Requirement 8: MFA enforcement (mandatory in Yokohama)
  • Requirement 10: Audit logging via sys_audit
  • Requirement 12: Policy management in GRC

For Requirement 10, querying the sys_audit table provides immutable logs for cardholder data access. Here's a practical GlideRecord example to fetch recent audits on FSO payment records, filtering for PCI-sensitive fields like account numbers.

var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_audit');
gr.addQuery('tablename', 'sn_bom_payment'); // FSO Payment table
gr.addQuery('fieldname', 'CONTAINS', 'account'); // Sensitive fields
gr.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>', gs.daysAgo(30)); // Last 30 days
gr.orderByDesc('sys_created_on');
gr.setLimit(100);
gr.query();
while (gr.next()) {
    gs.print('Audit: ' + gr.getDisplayValue('sys_created_on') + ' | User: ' + gr.getDisplayValue('userid') + ' | Old: ' + gr.oldvalue + ' | New: ' + gr.newvalue);
}

This query supports PCI-DSS audit reports, exportable to CSV for external auditors. For Requirement 7, role-based access to FSO tables like sn_bom_credit_card can be verified via script in Access Control Lists (ACLs).

In FSO environments, Flow Designer enhances PCI compliance by automating workflows for payment disputes. Consider this Flow Designer action example: Triggered on a new payment inquiry case (sn_bom_compl), it queries related customer accounts and assigns based on branch roles.

// Flow Designer Script Step: Get Customer Payment History
(function execute(inputs, outputs) {
    var caseId = inputs.case_sys_id;
    var grCase = new GlideRecord('sn_bom_compl');
    if (grCase.get(caseId)) {
        var customerId = grCase.getValue('customer');
        var grPayments = new GlideRecord('sn_bom_payment');
        grPayments.addQuery('customer', customerId);
        grPayments.addQuery('state', '!=', 'cancelled');
        grPayments.orderByDesc('sys_created_on');
        grPayments.setLimit(10);
        grPayments.query();
        
        var payments = [];
        while (grPayments.next()) {
            payments.push({
                number: grPayments.getDisplayValue('number'),
                amount: grPayments.getValue('amount'),
                status: grPayments.getDisplayValue('state')
            });
        }
        outputs.payments = JSON.stringify(payments);
    }
})(inputs, outputs);

This flow integrates with PCI workflows, ensuring restricted access (Req 7) while logging all actions (Req 10). For Basel III implementation, extend GRC with FSO tables to track liquidity coverage ratios (LCR) via custom indicators on sn_bom_account records.

Basel III requires robust risk data aggregation. Use this GlideRecord example in a scheduled script to aggregate exposures across loan portfolios:

var grLoans = new GlideRecord('sn_bom_loan');
grLoans.addQuery('state', 'active');
grLoans.query();
var totalExposure = 0;
while (grLoans.next()) {
    totalExposure += parseFloat(grLoans.getValue('exposure_amount') || 0);
}
gs.info('Total Basel III Exposure: $' + totalExposure.toLocaleString());

Combine these with GRC risk frameworks for automated Pillar 3 reporting. Overall, these code examples demonstrate how GlideRecord queries, business rules, and Flow Designer actions operationalize compliance in FSO, reducing manual effort while maintaining audit trails.

title: ServiceNow Healthcare Implementation: HIPAA, EMR Integration, and Clinical Workflows
excerpt: Build HIPAA-compliant ServiceNow implementations with EMR integration patterns, clinical device management, and healthcare-specific workflow automation.
content:
HIPAA Compliance Foundation

ServiceNow maintains HITRUST CSF certification and enters Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with covered entities.

Security Controls Required

  • Encryption: At-rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS 1.2+)
  • Access Control: Role-based with MFA
  • Audit Trails: All PHI access logged in sys_audit
  • Data Minimization: Collect only necessary PHI

Example: Enforcing Role-Based Access to PHI

The following example shows a server-side script (business rule or Script Include) that enforces role-based access to a clinical case record containing PHI. The pattern can be adapted for any table that stores PHI.

var grCase = new GlideRecord('sn_hcls_clinical_case');
if (grCase.get(current.sys_id)) {
    // Allow access only to users with a clinical role
    var userHasClinicalRole = gs.hasRole('sn_hcls.clinician') || gs.hasRole('sn_hcls.care_coordinator');

    if (!userHasClinicalRole) {
        // Log unauthorized access attempt for HIPAA auditing
        gs.warn('Unauthorized PHI access attempt by user {0} on case {1}',
                gs.getUserName(), grCase.number);

        // Mask sensitive fields before returning the record
        grCase.patient = '';
        grCase.diagnosis = '';
        grCase.notes = 'Access restricted per HIPAA policy.';
    }
}

Example: Writing a Custom PHI Access Audit Entry

Although standard field-level auditing is enabled through sys_audit, some implementations add a dedicated audit table for PHI access. The following GlideRecord example writes an audit record whenever a user opens a PHI-bearing record.

function logPhiAccess(targetTable, targetSysId, action) {
    // Custom PHI audit table (for example: x_hcls_phi_audit)
    var auditGr = new GlideRecord('x_hcls_phi_audit');
    auditGr.initialize();
    auditGr.user = gs.getUserID();
    auditGr.user_name = gs.getUserName();
    auditGr.target_table = targetTable;
    auditGr.target_sys_id = targetSysId;
    auditGr.action = action; // e.g. 'view', 'update', 'export'
    auditGr.access_time = new GlideDateTime();
    auditGr.insert();
}

// Example usage in an onDisplay business rule on a PHI table
if (current.isValidRecord()) {
    logPhiAccess(current.getTableName(), current.sys_id, 'view');
}

EMR Integration Patterns

Epic and Cerner integrations enable single-click issue reporting from clinical workflows, saving 7 minutes average per incident report.

Example: Creating an Incident from an EMR (Scripted REST API)

A common pattern is to expose a Scripted REST API that EMR systems (Epic, Cerner) can call when a clinician clicks a “Help” or “Report Issue” button. The example below shows a simple Scripted REST API resource script that creates an incident and associates it with a patient identifier from the EMR.

// Scripted REST API resource: POST /api/x_hcls/emr/incident
(function process(/*RESTAPIRequest*/ request, /*RESTAPIResponse*/ response) {
    var body = request.body.data;

    // Expect fields like: short_description, description, emr_patient_id, emr_user_id
    var inc = new GlideRecord('incident');
    inc.initialize();
    inc.short_description = body.short_description || 'Clinical issue reported from EMR';
    inc.description = body.description;
    inc.caller_id = gs.getUserID(); // or map from body.emr_user_id
    inc.u_emr_patient_id = body.emr_patient_id; // custom field to store EMR patient ID
    inc.u_emr_system = body.emr_system || 'Epic'; // track source system
    inc.category = 'inquiry';
    inc.subcategory = 'clinical';
    var sysId = inc.insert();

    var result = {
        incident_sys_id: sysId,
        incident_number: inc.number
    };

    response.setStatus(201);
    response.setBody(result);
})(request, response);

Example: Flow Designer Action to Enrich EMR Incidents

After the incident is created from an EMR, Flow Designer can enrich it with additional clinical context (for example, pulling patient demographic data from a Healthcare and Life Sciences table) and route it to the correct clinical support team.

// Example: Script step inside a Flow Designer action
// Input: incident_sys_id (String)
(function execute(inputs, outputs) {
    var inc = new GlideRecord('incident');
    if (!inc.get(inputs.incident_sys_id)) {
        gs.error('Incident not found for EMR enrichment: ' + inputs.incident_sys_id);
        return;
    }

    // Look up patient using u_emr_patient_id on incident
    var patientGr = new GlideRecord('sn_hcls_patient');
    patientGr.addQuery('u_emr_patient_id', inc.u_emr_patient_id);
    patientGr.query();
    if (patientGr.next()) {
        inc.u_patient_name = patientGr.name;
        inc.u_patient_dob = patientGr.date_of_birth;
        inc.u_patient_mrn = patientGr.u_mrn;
        inc.update();
    }

    // Route to clinical support assignment group based on EMR system
    var group = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
    group.addQuery('u_emr_support_for', inc.u_emr_system);
    group.query();
    if (group.next()) {
        inc.assignment_group = group.sys_id;
        inc.update();
    }

    outputs.incident_number = inc.number;
})(inputs, outputs);

Success Metrics

  • Omnicare: 90% first-contact resolution
  • Orbita: 70% reduction in nurse response times
  • Average: 7 minutes saved per incident report with EMR integration

Example: Reporting on Clinical Incident Resolution Metrics

To track healthcare implementation success, many teams build scheduled jobs or script-based reports that calculate metrics such as first-contact resolution and average time to resolve EMR-related incidents.

// Scheduled script example: calculate average resolution time for EMR incidents
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addEncodedQuery('u_emr_systemISNOTEMPTY^state=7'); // state=7 = Closed
gr.query();

var count = 0;
var totalDuration = 0; // in seconds

while (gr.next()) {
    // Work duration between opened_at and resolved_at
    var opened = new GlideDateTime(gr.opened_at);
    var resolved = new GlideDateTime(gr.resolved_at);
    var diffMs = GlideDateTime.subtract(resolved, opened).getNumericValue();
    totalDuration += (diffMs / 1000);
    count++;
}

if (count > 0) {
    var avgSeconds = totalDuration / count;
    var avgMinutes = Math.round(avgSeconds / 60);
    gs.info('Average EMR incident resolution time: ' + avgMinutes + ' minutes across ' + count + ' incidents.');
} else {
    gs.info('No closed EMR incidents found for metric calculation.');
}

These patterns help healthcare organizations operationalize HIPAA controls, standardize EMR integrations, and reliably measure the impact of ServiceNow on clinical workflows and patient care experiences.

title: ServiceNow Manufacturing: OT/IT Convergence and Connected Operations
excerpt: Implement ServiceNow for manufacturing with OT/IT convergence patterns, IoT integration, and field service optimization for Industry 4.0 environments.
content:
Overview

ServiceNow Manufacturing brings together Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT) on the Now Platform to support Industry 4.0 use cases such as connected operations, predictive maintenance, and secure OT/IT convergence. By extending the CMDB with ISA‑95 aligned equipment models, integrating IoT telemetry, and orchestrating field service workflows, manufacturers gain end‑to‑end visibility and control across plants, lines, and enterprise systems.

Operational Technology Management

Launched at Knowledge 2021, Operational Technology (OT) Management centralizes IT and OT assets in a single CMDB using ISA‑95 equipment model standards. OT Management builds on proven IT workflows—incident, problem, change, and request management—and applies them to production equipment, control systems, and industrial networks to improve availability, safety, and security.

OT Asset Modeling and CMDB

OT assets such as PLCs, HMIs, SCADA servers, historians, drives, and sensors are represented in the CMDB using OT‑specific classes and relationships. These configuration items (CIs) are related to manufacturing cells, production lines, and sites to provide a complete view of dependencies and service impact.

Example: creating an OT asset CI programmatically with GlideRecord:

var ci = new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci_ot_device');
ci.initialize();
ci.name = 'Filler PLC 01';
ci.u_equipment_id = 'PLC-FILL-01';
ci.u_site = 'Plant 1';
ci.u_line = 'Bottling Line 3';
ci.u_manufacturer = 'Example Automation';
ci.u_model = 'X1200';
ci.u_protocol = 'Modbus/TCP';
ci.insert();

OT Asset Discovery

To populate and maintain OT asset inventories, ServiceNow supports Service Graph Connectors and integrations with leading OT and security platforms. Common connectors include:

  • Claroty for OT security, asset discovery, and vulnerability data
  • Nozomi Networks for OT visibility, network monitoring, and anomaly detection
  • Forescout for device visibility across IT and OT endpoints

These connectors normalize asset data into the CMDB, enrich CIs with security posture and connectivity details, and enable manufacturers to correlate incidents, vulnerabilities, and changes across both IT and OT domains.

Example: scheduled import pattern for connector data:

var imp = new GlideRecord('u_ot_import_queue');
imp.initialize();
imp.source = 'claroty';
imp.payload = current.u_raw_json;  // from MID Server or integration
imp.state = 'ready';
imp.insert();

IT/OT Convergence Patterns

With OT assets modeled in the same CMDB as IT, manufacturers can implement convergence patterns such as:

  • Unified incident workflows where a single incident record coordinates plant maintenance, OT engineers, and IT network teams
  • Coordinated change management for firmware updates, control logic changes, and network configuration changes with risk assessment and approvals
  • Shared security operations where OT alerts feed into Security Incident Response, enabling consistent triage, containment, and post‑incident review

Example: automatically routing OT incidents to the appropriate support group:

var inc = new GlideRecord('incident');
inc.initialize();
inc.short_description = 'Line 3 PLC communication loss';
inc.category = 'OT';
inc.cmdb_ci = ci.sys_id; // reference to OT CI
inc.assignment_group = 'OT Support';
inc.impact = 1;
inc.urgency = 1;
inc.insert();

OT Security and Governance

OT Management also supports security and governance by integrating vulnerability, configuration, and network telemetry from OT tools into ServiceNow workflows. Security teams can:

  • Prioritize vulnerabilities based on asset criticality and production impact
  • Coordinate patching or mitigation windows with plant operations via change requests
  • Track exceptions, compensating controls, and audit evidence for compliance frameworks

Connected Operations with IoT

Connected operations extend OT Management with IoT data ingestion, analytics, and workflow triggers. Manufacturers can collect telemetry from sensors, gateways, and edge devices using MQTT, HTTP, and other protocols to enable real‑time monitoring and predictive maintenance.

IoT Data Ingestion (MQTT and HTTP)

IoT gateways and devices commonly publish telemetry, alarms, and status updates using MQTT topics or HTTP APIs. ServiceNow can subscribe to MQTT brokers via a gateway or use IntegrationHub and custom endpoints to receive data and convert it into events, alerts, or work orders.

Example: processing an HTTP POST from an IoT gateway (Scripted REST API):

var body = request.body.data;
var payload = JSON.parse(body);

// Example payload:
// { "asset_id": "PLC-FILL-01", "temp": 78.2, "vibration": 6.1, "status": "warning" }

var ci = new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci_ot_device');
ci.addQuery('u_equipment_id', payload.asset_id);
ci.query();
if (ci.next()) {
    // Create an event for Operations Management
    var evt = new GlideRecord('em_event');
    evt.initialize();
    evt.source = 'IoT Gateway';
    evt.node = ci.sys_id;
    evt.type = 'threshold';
    evt.severity = payload.status == 'warning' ? 3 : 2;
    evt.message_key = payload.asset_id + '_vibration';
    evt.description = 'Vibration level ' + payload.vibration + ' for ' + ci.name;
    evt.insert();
}

Real‑Time Equipment Monitoring

Once IoT data is ingested, ServiceNow Event Management and AIOps can detect anomalies, correlate events, and open incidents or maintenance tasks. Dashboards and digital twins can visualize machine status, OEE metrics, and production KPIs across plants and lines.

Example: creating a maintenance task when repeated alerts occur:

var alert = current; // em_alert
if (alert.count >= 3 && alert.resource_type == 'cmdb_ci_ot_device') {
    var wo = new GlideRecord('wm_order');
    wo.initialize();
    wo.short_description = 'Investigate repeated vibration alerts for ' + alert.resource;
    wo.cmdb_ci = alert.resource;
    wo.u_failure_mode = 'High vibration';
    wo.assignment_group = 'Plant Maintenance';
    wo.insert();
}

Predictive Maintenance and Analytics

By combining historical IoT data, work order history, and asset attributes, manufacturers can implement predictive maintenance. Models can predict failure risk, recommend optimal maintenance windows, and automatically create work orders or changes before breakdowns occur.

Field Service and Connected Workforce

ServiceNow Field Service Management (FSM) closes the loop between detected OT or IoT issues and on‑site remediation. When an alert or incident is raised, FSM can:

  • Automatically generate work orders with asset details, location, and safety instructions
  • Schedule the right technician based on skills, certifications, and proximity
  • Provide mobile access to procedures, parts lists, and digital checklists

Example: creating a field service work order from an OT incident:

var inc = current; // incident
if (inc.category == 'OT' && inc.cmdb_ci) {
    var wo = new GlideRecord('wm_order');
    wo.initialize();
    wo.short_description = 'On-site investigation for OT incident ' + inc.number;
    wo.incident = inc.sys_id;
    wo.cmdb_ci = inc.cmdb_ci;
    wo.u_required_skill = 'OT Controls';
    wo.state = 'dispatched';
    wo.insert();
}

Manufacturing Success Metrics

Manufacturers adopting OT/IT convergence and connected operations on ServiceNow typically measure value across reliability, performance, and cost dimensions. Representative outcomes include:

  • 25% efficiency increase in field operations through optimized dispatch, standardized procedures, and mobile workflows
  • $3M cost reduction from optimized maintenance strategies, reduced truck rolls, and lower spare parts consumption
  • 40% reduction in unplanned downtime by shifting from reactive to predictive maintenance and improving OT incident response

Additional qualitative benefits often include stronger collaboration between IT, OT, and security teams, faster onboarding of new plants or lines, and better retention of institutional knowledge through digitized workflows.

Conclusion

ServiceNow Manufacturing, anchored by Operational Technology Management, IoT‑enabled connected operations, and integrated field service, provides a unified platform for OT/IT convergence in Industry 4.0 environments. By centralizing OT and IT assets in the CMDB, ingesting real‑time telemetry via MQTT and HTTP, and orchestrating end‑to‑end workflows from detection to resolution, manufacturers can increase asset availability, reduce unplanned downtime, and optimize maintenance and field operations. Implementing these patterns on the Now Platform helps create a resilient, data‑driven manufacturing enterprise that can continuously improve performance, quality, and safety across the entire value chain.

title: ServiceNow Government: FedRAMP High Implementation and Citizen Services
excerpt: Deploy ServiceNow in government environments with FedRAMP High authorization, citizen service playbooks, and accessibility compliance patterns.
content:
FedRAMP Authorization Levels

ServiceNow maintains FedRAMP High Authorization with 400+ security controls:

  • Government Community Cloud (GCC): FedRAMP High and DoD IL-4
  • National Security Cloud (NSC): DoD IL-5

The following example shows how a federal agency might programmatically retrieve only FedRAMP High–authorized ServiceNow instances from a custom inventory table for reporting and continuous monitoring.

var inv = new GlideRecord('u_system_inventory');
inv.addQuery('u_fedramp_level', 'HIGH');
inv.addQuery('u_environment_type', 'GCC'); // GovCommunityCloud only
inv.query();

while (inv.next()) {
    gs.info('FedRAMP High system: ' + inv.u_system_name +
            ' | ATO status: ' + inv.u_ato_status +
            ' | POA&M count: ' + inv.u_poam_open_count);
}

You can also use a scheduled script to verify that all FedRAMP High systems have an assigned Authorizing Official (AO) and an active Authority to Operate (ATO), which supports monthly POA&M reporting.

var sys = new GlideRecord('u_system_inventory');
sys.addQuery('u_fedramp_level', 'HIGH');
sys.query();

while (sys.next()) {
    if (gs.nil(sys.u_authorizing_official) || sys.u_ato_expiration < gs.nowDateTime()) {
        var poam = new GlideRecord('u_poam_item');
        poam.initialize();
        poam.u_system = sys.getUniqueValue();
        poam.u_title = 'Missing AO or expired ATO for FedRAMP High system';
        poam.u_severity = 'High';
        poam.u_status = 'Open';
        poam.insert();
    }
}

Public Sector Digital Services (PSDS)

Pre-built playbooks accelerate citizen service delivery:

  • Service Request: General citizen inquiries
  • Information Request: FOIA with document redaction
  • Eligibility and Benefits: Automated eligibility determination
  • Licensing and Permitting: Application processing
  • Grants Management: Award lifecycle

The following GlideRecord example demonstrates how a public sector agency could automatically route Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests to a specialized queue based on request type and sensitivity, while tagging the record for redaction workflow in PSDS.

var req = new GlideRecord('sn_ps_citizen_request');
req.addQuery('u_channel', 'online_portal');
req.addQuery('u_request_type', 'FOIA');
req.addQuery('u_state', 'new');
req.query();

while (req.next()) {
    // Route to FOIA work queue
    req.assignment_group = 'FOIA_Request_Processing';
    req.u_requires_redaction = true;
    req.u_service_playbook = 'foia_information_request';
    req.state = 'in_progress';
    req.update();
}

To orchestrate citizen service delivery using Flow Designer, you can build a flow that triggers on new PSDS requests, evaluates eligibility criteria, and sends automated notifications. The pseudo-code below represents a scripted action that might be used inside a Flow Designer Action to determine benefit eligibility.

/* Flow Designer Script Step: Evaluate Eligibility */
(function execute(inputs, outputs) {
    var app = new GlideRecord('sn_ps_eligibility_case');
    if (!app.get(inputs.case_sys_id)) {
        outputs.is_eligible = false;
        outputs.reason = 'Case not found';
        return;
    }

    var age = parseInt(app.u_applicant_age, 10);
    var income = parseFloat(app.u_household_income);

    if (age >= 65 && income <= 40000) {
        outputs.is_eligible = true;
        outputs.benefit_tier = 'Senior_Low_Income';
    } else if (income <= 25000) {
        outputs.is_eligible = true;
        outputs.benefit_tier = 'Low_Income';
    } else {
        outputs.is_eligible = false;
        outputs.reason = 'Does not meet eligibility thresholds';
    }
})(inputs, outputs);

Accessibility Compliance

ServiceNow is WCAG 2.1 AA conformant with:

  • 24 out-of-box languages
  • Screen reader compatibility
  • Keyboard navigation support
  • High contrast themes

The following example adds an accessibility tag to citizen-facing records when a user indicates they require assistive technology, allowing agencies to prioritize reasonable accommodations and accessible communications.

var reqAcc = new GlideRecord('sn_ps_citizen_request');
reqAcc.addQuery('u_accessibility_required', true);
reqAcc.addQuery('u_accessibility_flagged', false);
reqAcc.query();

while (reqAcc.next()) {
    reqAcc.u_accessibility_flagged = true;
    reqAcc.u_preferred_contact_mode = 'accessible_email'; // Accessible channel
    reqAcc.update();
}

For custom portals, use a Script Include to enforce accessible language selection and high-contrast themes for authenticated government users with recorded accessibility preferences.

var AccessibilityPrefs = Class.create();
AccessibilityPrefs.prototype = {
    initialize: function() {},

    applyUserAccessibilitySettings: function(userSysId) {
        var prefs = new GlideRecord('u_user_accessibility_pref');
        if (!prefs.get('u_user', userSysId)) {
            return;
        }

        // Enforce WCAG-friendly theme and language
        gs.setProperty('glide.ui.theme', prefs.u_high_contrast ? 'hc_theme' : 'standard');
        gs.getSession().putProperty('glide.user.language', prefs.u_language || 'en');
    },

    type: 'AccessibilityPrefs'
};
